newsitem.title: USA: SEC staff targets Orange County bond attorney.
newsitem.headline: SEC staff targets Orange County bond attorney.

text.p: Securities and Exchange Commission staff has informed one of Orange County, Calif.,'s former bond attorneys that she is a potential target in their probe into the bankruptcy, her attorney said Friday.
Jean Costanza, a partner with the law firm of LeBoeuf Lamb Greene & MacRae, received a so-called Wells notice several months ago and responded in August, the attorney confirmed.
A Wells notice informs its recipient that the SEC staff intends to recommend enforcement action to commissioners.
"Jean Costanza got a Wells and we have made a submission to the commission," said her attorney, Gary Cohen.
Cohen, an attorney with the San Francisco law firm of Keker and Van Nest, declined further comment on Costanza's case, but said LeBoeuf Lamb had not received a Wells notice.
For months, it has been widely reported that Costanza was one of many targets in the SEC investigation, which followed Orange County's unprecedented bankruptcy filing.
SEC officials in Los Angeles were not immediately available to comment on the case. In the past, SEC officials have refused to comment.
Several other bond professionals have also received Wells notices.
Orange County filed for protection under Chapter 9 of the federal Bankruptcy Code on December 6, 1994 after sustaining investment losses of more than $1.6 billion.
The county emerged from bankruptcy in June of this year.

Before it emerged from bankruptcy, the county sued LeBoeuf Lamb and Costanza, alleging the firm participated in the issuance of official statements for bond issues that contained misleading information and omissions about the county investment portfolio.
